column3: NKJV has “I would have told you. I go,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text adds “that,” reading “would I have told you that I go …?”
NKJV has “and the way you know,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “you know the way.”
NKJV has “If you had known Me, you would have known,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “If you have known Me, you will know.”
NKJV has “who dwells in Me does the works,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “dwelling in Me does His works.”
NKJV includes “Me” after the second “believe,” following the Textus Receptus.
NKJV has “My Father,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the Father.”
NKJV lacks “Me” after “ask,” as does the Textus Receptus; the critical text includes it.
NKJV has the imperative “keep,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the future “you will keep.”
NKJV has “abide,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “be.” “Ask” is rendered “pray.”
NKJV includes “I said” and “My Father,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “because I am going to the Father, for the Father is greater.”
